public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 851

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/851](https://www.erdosproblems.com/851)
- [Pr26] D. Price and GPT-5.2 Pro, [Erdős problem 851](https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e) (2026)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos851

/--
`TwoPowAddSet r` is the set of integers of the form `2^k+n`, where `k ≥ 0` and `n` has at most `r`
prime divisors.
-/
def TwoPowAddSet (r : ℕ) := {(2 ^ k + n) | (k : ℕ) (n : ℕ) (_ : n.primeFactors.card ≤ r)}

/-- The set of integers of the form `2^k+p`, where `k ≥ 0` and `p` is prime. -/
def twoPowAddPrimeSet : Set ℕ := {(2 ^ k + p) | (k : ℕ) (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime)}

/--
The set of integers of the form `2^k+p` (where `p` is prime) has positive lower density.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_851.variants.romanoff : 0 < Set.lowerDensity twoPowAddPrimeSet := by
  sorry

/--
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some $r \ll_\epsilon 1$ such that the density of integers of the
form $2^k+n$, where $k \geq 0$ and $n$ has at most $r$ prime divisors, is at least $1-\epsilon$?

This was proved affirmatively by Price and GPT-5.2 Pro [Pr26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos851.lean#L37"]
theorem erdos_851 (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) : ∃ r,
    1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity := by
  sorry

end Erdos851

reformulations.difference: Erdős's literal question [Er85c, p.75] asks: for every ε > 0, is there an r such that the lower density of {2^k + q : k ≥ 0, q ≥ 1, ω(q) < r} is greater than (or at least) 1 − ε? The Lean statement differs in form in four ways. (i) It quantifies only over ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1. (ii) `TwoPowAddSet r` admits n = 0, because Mathlib has `Nat.primeFactors 0 = ∅`. So every power of two lies in every `TwoPowAddSet r`, although mathematically every prime divides 0, and the `TwoPowAddSet` docstring says "n has at most r prime divisors". (iii) It uses `n.primeFactors.card ≤ r`, where Er85c writes ω(q_r) < r; erdosproblems.com says "at most r". (iv) It asserts the affirmative answer as a bare theorem rather than `answer(True) ↔ …`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (i) For ε ≥ 1 the claim holds for any r, since `Set.lowerDensity_nonneg` gives lowerDensity ≥ 0 ≥ 1 − ε. (ii) Let S'_r = {2^k + q : q ≥ 1, ω(q) ≤ r}. Then S'_r ⊆ TwoPowAddSet r ⊆ S'_{max r 1} ∪ {1}, because 2^(j+1) = 2^j + 2^j with ω(2^j) ≤ 1, and 2^0 = 1. Lower density is monotone under inclusion. It is unchanged by adding one point: the partial density rises by at most 1/b → 0 (`Filter.liminf_add_le`). (iii) The sets are monotone in r and r is existentially quantified, so shifting r by one turns ω < r into ω ≤ r and back. (iv) Strict versus non-strict comparison with 1 − ε is absorbed by the ∀ ε quantifier (apply the hypothesis at ε/2), and `answer(True) ↔ P` is equivalent to P. I proved in /workspace/review/equiv.lean that (∀ ε ∈ Ioo 0 1, ∃ r, 1 − ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity) ↔ (∀ ε > 0, ∃ r, 1 − ε ≤ lowerDensity {x | ∃ k q, 0 < q ∧ q.primeFactors.card < r ∧ 2^k + q = x}), and the same with `<` in place of `≤` against 1 − ε. `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

review.notes:
I found no misformalization. Both theorems state what the source poses.

1. Density notion and ω. erdosproblems.com says \"density\" and \"n has at most r prime divisors\". The original source it cites, [Er85c, p.75], is explicit on both points: \"(ω(n) denotes the number of distinct prime factors of n). By the way is it true that to every ε > 0 [there is an r] so that the lower density of the integers of the form 2^k + q_r [is > / ≥] 1 − ε?\" So `Set.lowerDensity` and `n.primeFactors.card` are literally the source's notions, not modelling choices. The same page of Er85c says \"Romanoff proved that the lower density of the integers which can be written in the form 2^k + p is positive\", which matches `erdos_851.variants.romanoff`.

2. Status. erdosproblems.com records the problem as PROVED (Price with GPT-5.2 Pro; Tao confirmed the proof in the forum). This agrees with `research solved`. The cited Overleaf proof actually establishes the stronger Ω version: lower natural density ≥ 1 − ε for {2^k + n : n ≥ 1, Ω(n) ≤ r}, and its Remark notes that this implies the ω version. A stronger Ω variant (via `ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors`) could be added, but its absence is not a defect.

3. `formal_proof` record. Line 37 of the pinned plby/lean-proofs file states exactly `theorem erdos_851 (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) : ∃ r : ℕ, 1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity`. Its `TwoPowAddSet` (in Erdos851/Basic.lean) and `lowerDensity`/`partialDensity` (in Util/Density.lean) are verbatim copies of the FC definitions. I fetched the whole 69-file import tree outside Mathlib and found no `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide` or `axiom` declarations. I did not compile that project (Lean v4.33.0 with external dependencies), so kernel-checking of the proof is unverified here; the record is consistent with the source.

4. Boundary checks in Lean. `TwoPowAddSet` elaborates to `{x | ∃ k n, ∃ (_ : n.primeFactors.card ≤ r), 2 ^ k + n = x}`. The value 0 is in no `TwoPowAddSet r`, and 1 is in `TwoPowAddSet 0` via n = 0. A computable membership test proved equal to the set shows that `TwoPowAddSet 3` contains every m < 20000 except 0; `TwoPowAddSet 2` contains 19894 of them and `TwoPowAddSet 1` 11816. This is consistent with the numerics posted with the problem. The statement is not trivially provable.

5. Style only. The question is stated as the bare affirmative theorem rather than `answer(True) ↔ …`. This is equivalent and not a finding.

6. Sandbox. `lakefile.toml` and `run/` in the checkout were modified at 12:21, before this review started; I changed nothing under /opt/formal-conjectures.
